copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Croatia v Ghana in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, and the model and the market disagree on the Croatia side by +12.5pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Public Elo rates Croatia 240 points higher than the other side (Croatia 1860, Ghana 1620). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Croatia to win at 67%, the draw at 16%, and Ghana to win at 17%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Croatia sits at 67% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Croatia to win at 55%, the draw at 26%, and Ghana to win at 18%. Polymarket has Croatia at 55%, which prices out at American odds of −122; the model has the same side at 67%. The +12.5pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Croatia the lower bound is 58%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 32 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the Croatia side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Croatia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.5pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Croatia look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 67% vs market 55% — a +12.5pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Croatia v Ghana · the model leans Croatia
